tracks.title: 1996 (An Extension of Me)
tracks.loreNote: The song establishes the backstory of Jordan's birth year, 1996, and the origins of his mother's controlling nature. Aubrie Sinclair's worldview was entirely shaped by her one sexual encounter with David Fuller, which she falsely believed would lead to marriage. After he abandoned her, she developed a deep-seated bitterness and resentment toward the world. Consequently, she views her son, Aubrey "Jordan" Fuller, not as an individual, but as her property and a literal extension of herself. This mindset drives her to keep him isolated, treating the outside world as a threat to maintain his dependence on her.

tracks.title: The Dependency Loop
tracks.loreNote: This track delves into the specific mechanics of Aubrie Sinclair's control over her son. She deliberately weaponized "care" by refusing to teach Jordan basic life skills, such as how to dress himself or tie his shoes, forcing him to rely entirely on her for survival. By framing the outside world as dangerous and positioning herself as his sole protector and provider, she created a suffocating "cage of comfort." The song also touches upon her medical deception—keeping him unvaccinated and isolated from doctors—ensuring her absolute authority over his physical and mental well-being to guarantee he would never leave her.

tracks.title: Inappropriate (The Opt-Out)
tracks.loreNote: This track explores Aubrie Sinclair's deliberate strategy to keep Jordan ignorant about human anatomy, relationships, and sexuality. By repeatedly opting him out of mandatory school health and family life classes—labeling the curriculum "inappropriate" for him—she weaponized his innocence. Her goal was to ensure he remained isolated, dependent, and entirely under her control, shielding him from any knowledge that might lead to romantic connections, personal autonomy, or an understanding of his own body.

tracks.title: The Silly College Experiment (Astrophysics)
tracks.loreNote: This track explores Aubrie Sinclair's manipulative mindset regarding Jordan's enrollment at Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute. She views his desire for higher education as a "silly college experiment" and deliberately sets him up to fail by selecting Astrophysics—a highly complex and mathematically demanding major—as his degree path. Her intention is not for him to succeed, but to use this "insurmountable mountain" to prove his incompetence, shatter his confidence, and force him to return home, cementing his lifelong dependency on her.

tracks.title: Route Four-Sixty (The Seven-Hour Drive)
tracks.loreNote: This track captures the tense, seven-hour journey from the humid flatlands of Hampton Roads to the rolling mountains of the New River Valley for college move-in day. Traveling westward along U.S. Route 460, Jordan is trapped in the passenger seat, forced to endure a relentless stream of anxious instructions and oppressive rules from his mother, Aubrie Sinclair. Instead of feeling the excitement of a new beginning, he feels like a prisoner being transported to an academic jail, overwhelmed by panic and the suffocating fear that he is destined to fail her "silly college experiment."

tracks.title: Stranded (A Real College Kid)
tracks.loreNote: This track captures Jordan's profound isolation and despair during his first night alone in his dorm room at CPI. After his mother departs with the hollow praise of him being a "real college kid" and "living on your own," the stark reality sets in: she deliberately never taught him fundamental life skills. Unable to reach a wall outlet, change his own clothes, or even tie his shoes, Jordan realizes he is completely stranded in his own space. The song reflects his crushing realization that her words weren't a genuine statement of pride, but rather a cruel confirmation that she had set him up to fail and was glad to be rid of the burden.

tracks.title: Clerical Error (A New Light)
tracks.loreNote: This track marks the pivotal turning point in Jordan's life. Due to a university housing crisis and a clerical error that mistook his legal name, "Aubrey," for a female, he is assigned to a handicap-accessible suite with five young women. On official move-in day, the cacophony of the hallway and the sudden realization of the mix-up trigger a severe autistic meltdown. Rather than reacting with judgment or fear, his suitemate Aubrie Jean Kelly—who is also autistic—immediately recognizes his distress. She steps forward to ground him, wrapping him in a firm, protective embrace. This profound act of unconditional kindness is the very first he has ever experienced, sparking a "new light" in his dark world and laying the foundation for their extraordinary chosen family.

tracks.title: System.Crash(Meltdown_01)
tracks.loreNote: This track thrusts the listener directly into the chaotic sensory overload of Jordan's first major autistic meltdown in the story. Triggered by the deafening noise of freshman move-in day, the sudden presence of female strangers in his suite, and the terrifying realization of the housing mix-up over his legal name "Aubrey," his mind experiences a complete system failure. Unable to process the compounding stressors or execute an escape, he is paralyzed by panic, rocking in his wheelchair and covering his ears as his world temporarily shatters around him.

tracks.title: The Anchor Holds (Aubrie's Theme)
tracks.loreNote: This track shifts the perspective to Aubrie Jean Kelly during the chaotic events of move-in day. Being autistic herself, Aubrie instantly recognizes that Jordan's frantic rocking and covering of his ears is not an act of aggression, but a severe sensory and emotional overload. Gently explaining to her parents that he is simply overwhelmed, she steps into the room and takes control of the situation. By calmly asking for his consent and providing a firm, grounding embrace, she acts as a living anchor for his crashing system. This profound, unconditional act of care marks the very first genuine hug Jordan has ever received in his life, cementing Aubrie's role as his primary safe harbor.

tracks.title: The Same Constellations
tracks.loreNote: Following the chaotic events of move-in day and Jordan's subsequent meltdown, he and Aubrie share a quiet moment of connection. Jordan nervously reveals his assigned major, Astrophysics—a subject his mother deliberately chose as an insurmountable trap to ensure he would fail her "silly college experiment." He fully expects Aubrie to pity him or confirm his inadequacy. Instead, her face lights up as she joyfully declares, "Me too!" For Aubrie, the cosmos and the laws of physics are a logical, predictable sanctuary from a confusing world. Her genuine excitement shatters his mother's manipulative trap, transforming his greatest academic fear into a shared passion and a fragile, dawning hope for the future.

tracks.title: The Naming (A Joke That Stuck)
tracks.loreNote: This track represents a crucial moment of empowerment and self-determination for the protagonist. During a quiet conversation with Aubrie Jean Kelly, he explains the origin of his legal first name, "Aubrey." His abusive mother, whose name is Aubrie, gave him the gender-neutral name as a cruel joke that ultimately became permanent on his birth certificate. Recognizing the shared name as a source of his lifelong trauma, daily confusion, and the catalyst for the dorm room mix-up, he makes his first true act of defiance. He announces that he despises the name "Aubrey" and chooses to go by his middle name, "Jordan," officially shedding his old identity and stepping into his new life.

tracks.title: A Different Kind of Constellation (The Pact)
tracks.loreNote: This track details the radical and beautiful formation of the group's poly-affectionate dynamic. After Lauren is publicly humiliated and cruelly dumped by her ex-boyfriend, Jordan steps in to comfort her, offering her unconditional tenderness and a safe embrace. Watching this, Aubrie Jean realizes she feels absolutely no jealousy—only a profound sense of rightness and protective care. She proposes an unconventional solution: rather than competing for Jordan and treating him like a prize to be won, the single women of the suite (Aubrie, Madison, Zoe, and Lauren) agree to share his romantic affection as co-equals. Hannah, devoted to her boyfriend Mark, lovingly opts out of the romantic aspect but cements her role as his platonic best friend and official hug-giver. They cease to be roommates and become a "constellation" of support, fundamentally defining the open-hearted terms of Jordan's new life.

tracks.title: The Cut Cord (No Service)
tracks.loreNote: This track depicts Aubrie Sinclair's vindictive retaliation after Jordan refuses to leave his new family and return home for Fall Break. Having been denied physical access to him at the dorm, she executes a calculated strike to isolate him by terminating his cell phone service. Her goal is to cut his digital cord to the outside world, punishing his independence and attempting to prove that he cannot survive without her financial control and authority. She believes this forced isolation will make him come crawling back.

tracks.title: [LOGISTICS] (The Buddy System)
tracks.loreNote: When Aubrie Sinclair cuts off Jordan's cellular service in a malicious attempt to isolate him, his chosen family immediately counters with a brilliant logistical defense. Zoe utilizes a VoIP app to secure a new, private phone number for Jordan that operates entirely over the university's WiFi, effectively bypassing his mother's financial control. To protect him when he is between buildings and off the network, Madison creates the "Jordan Comms" group chat and institutes a strict "Buddy System," ensuring he is never without a trusted family member by his side. Musically, this track is a turning point: it introduces bright, hopeful 80s synth-rock elements that actively push back against the dark, industrial tones of his past, symbolizing his new family's network successfully defeating his mother's oppressive control.

tracks.title: Sanctuary (The Thanksgiving Exodus)
tracks.loreNote: When Aubrie Sinclair sends a Thanksgiving ultimatum demanding Jordan return to Hampton Roads, his chosen family orchestrates a swift escape. Utilizing the Maroon Express, the group travels to Christiansburg, Virginia, to seek refuge at the home of Zoe's family, the Brooks. Although it is just a short bus ride down the road, to Jordan, the journey feels like an exodus deep into the Appalachian mountains, far beyond his mother's oppressive grip. Upon arriving at the house on a hill, he is met with immediate, unconditional acceptance. Laura Brooks, Zoe's mother, doesn't see a burden or a broken child; she simply sees her daughter's friend—her "daughter's boy." For the first time in his life, Jordan experiences the warmth and safety of a true family home, cementing the Brooks' residence as his ultimate sanctuary.

tracks.title: Guardianship (The Summons)
tracks.loreNote: Back at CPI for the Spring semester, Jordan's hard-won peace is violently interrupted when he receives an ominous email summoning him alone to Hall Director Kelsey's office at 3:00 PM. Waiting inside is a Montgomery County Sheriff's Deputy. When the uniformed officer formally addresses him by his full legal name, "Aubrey Jordan Fuller," the trauma of his mother's abuse and the terrifying realization of her reach triggers a severe autistic meltdown. Kelsey expertly steps in to de-escalate the situation, but the damage is done. The envelope contains a court summons: Aubrie Sinclair has filed a petition in Norfolk to have Jordan declared legally incompetent and placed under her guardianship, launching a desperate, malicious legal war to drag him back under her control.

tracks.title: The Bluewater Bunker
tracks.loreNote: This track details the group's frantic flight from Blacksburg to Bluewater, Virginia—a fictional town located near the real-world interchange of I-77 and US-58—after Aubrie Sinclair's private investigator discovers their location at the Hotel at Poly. Taking refuge in Madison Scott's childhood home, the group creates the "Bluewater Bunker." While the house provides a necessary safe haven from the looming court case and the immediate threat of the PI, it presents a grueling physical challenge for Jordan. The inaccessible environment forces him to endure humiliating physical struggles just to navigate the space. However, anchored by the presence of his "safe people," Aubrie and Madison, the temporary fortress becomes a place of profound emotional security despite the overwhelming physical hardships and anxiety.

tracks.title: Dismissed (With Prejudice)
tracks.loreNote: This track serves as the triumphant climax to the first half of Jordan's journey, detailing his definitive victory in a Norfolk courtroom. Facing his abusive mother and her sleazebag lawyer, Jordan is backed by an unshakeable wall of sixteen family members filling the gallery. His lawyer, Ms. Gable, systematically dismantles the petition for guardianship and conservatorship not with emotion, but with undeniable facts: Jordan's Dean's List transcript, his independently filed tax returns, and his proactive healthcare decisions. After Jordan testifies to his own safety and independence, the furious judge reprimands his mother for wasting the court's time and dismisses the case "with prejudice." The ruling permanently severs Aubrie Sinclair's legal reach, granting Jordan absolute freedom.
